references.text: The book of Ruth describes a practical application of the levirate laws, where Boaz goes to the city gate and the elders to settle the matter of redemption duty, just as described in Deuteronomy
The custom of removing a sandal as a sign of giving up the right of redemption is described, which connects to the ritual in Deuteronomy 25
Onan refused to fulfill his duty as Tamar's brother-in-law to raise offspring for his brother, which is the very core of the levirate marriage laws
The Sadducees cite the levirate law when they ask Jesus a question about the resurrection, referring to the duty to raise offspring for a brother
Mark recounts the Sadducees' reference to Moses' law on levirate marriage, where a brother is to take his deceased brother's wife
Luke describes the Sadducees' question, which refers to the levirate law about raising offspring for a brother
